description.value: Wonowon Lodge is a large camp-style accommodation at Mile 101 of the Alaska Highway in remote northern BC, operating primarily as a workers' lodge for the oil and gas industry with 289 suites ranging from standard rooms to full well-site configurations with private kitchens. The facility includes a fully catered dining room, recreation centre with pool table and ping pong, two fitness rooms, and laundry. For Alaska Highway touring cyclists, it represents one of the few substantial accommodation and meal options in this isolated stretch between Fort St. John and Fort Nelson.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website confirms a real, operating lodge at Mile 101 of the Alaska Highway with 289 rooms, primarily serving oil and gas workers ('wellsite rooms', 'per man-day' pricing). Laundry is explicitly confirmed ('Full laundry', 'laundry facilities-supplies included'), and Wi-Fi is confirmed ('Wireless broadband high-speed internet is available throughout the camp'), corroborating the OSM internet_access=yes tag. No bike-specific amenities (secure storage, bike procedure, e-bike charging, tools, pump) are mentioned anywhere on the site.
concerns: Name capitalization discrepancy: OSM records 'Wonowon Lodge' but the website consistently uses 'WonoWon Lodge'.

Lodge primarily targets oil and gas industry workers ('wellsite rooms', 'per man-day' pricing, 12 wellsites); unclear whether walk-in or transient touring cyclist bookings are accepted — may warrant a call to confirm availability for individual travellers.
